findings.explanation: The root composes the three immediate inputs/software repositories and contains the manuscript, statistics interface, figures and image archive. Makefile and main.tex use that hierarchy. The upstream acquisition locator is a separate reachability qualification; the selected statistical inputs are nested beneath the root.

Following root → data/raw_eyegaze reveals a nested src/lab-eyetracking gitlink whose URL is a host-local path. This is an actual locator defect within the explicitly linked graph, while the selected TSV inputs are already in the phase2 dataset. Partial is defensible for that broader graph, without claiming that the selected paper input retrieval failed.

The paper computation installs its external Python/rendering packages inside the image and installs REMoDNaV from the tracked software module. The linked older package also declares its runtime libraries. This supports software inclusion; the failure to freeze the historic label environment belongs to the more specific environment criteria.

An independent frozen-tree read confirms ordinary Git blobs for code, manuscript and configuration and gitlinks for components. Deliberately omitted evidence-package files do not show untracked author work. The assessment correctly rejects the dirty-checkout heuristic for this committed-state question.

The root tree has six image-archive symlinks; frozen metadata identifies annex keys for them, including the large layer. The phase2 README explains the Git metadata/git-annex payload split. These are concrete uses of large-content version control; they do not establish current payload availability.

The result record binds container/image as an extra input. In contrast, the label record runs compute_all.sh without an environment identity; a sampled shipped event TSV last changed in that record. I also independently traced velhist.svg to the ordinary 2020 commit and verified its generating function is omitted from main. Partial captures specific remaining provenance gaps.

The root has substantial installation/usage instructions, but its all-results promise exceeds the command dispatch. The native entry-point probe reproduces its false match on the prose phrase make changes. An additional real gap is root → labels → README: it still instructs Condor submission of old preprocessing/detection files absent from the frozen tree, whereas the recorded computation uses compute_all.sh.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep partial and add the stale linked label instructions as a concrete second documentation failure; do not cite the make-changes regex hit as a defect.

findings.explanation: The main starting command is identifiable, yet its -s -f -r -m dispatch never calls quality_stats although main.tex uses velhist.pdf. The label module also offers a README route inconsistent with its recorded Bash route. The root does have an entry point, so partial is more accurate than absent/unmet.

The container cleanup paths and in-container mount are not host-path defects. Partial is independently supported more directly by the linked label submit generators, which hardcode a personal working directory and a system Python executable. The limited native path probe confirms both submit-script hits. The assessment missed these scripts and relied only on the upstream module URL.
findings.suggested_correction: Keep partial, but cite the two label submit generators as executable path assumptions and distinguish them from the currently recorded compute_all.sh route.

findings.explanation: The image recipe covers the paper analysis stack. The label loop instead uses ambient python and PYTHONPATH, and its package declaration does not define the interpreter/system environment for the shipped labels. This establishes a component-specific gap rather than a claim that no dependency specification exists anywhere.

Partial is supported for the whole linked object: the label submission route embeds a machine-specific directory, Python 2.7 and inherited environment; the root documents substantially more of its Docker route. The adapter does expose PATH/account assumptions, but external installation pages were not frozen, so their failure to explain Docker permissions cannot be established here.
findings.suggested_correction: Prefer the concrete linked-script host assumptions as the principal evidence. Qualify the Docker-permission claim as a local-documentation gap, since the linked installation guidance was not inspected.

findings.explanation: The met rationale assesses only the root requirements despite including linked label production elsewhere. The label README advertises a Condor pipeline with preprocessing/detection programs that are absent at this revision; its surviving submit generators additionally assume Python 2.7 and an inherited host environment. There is no coherent requirements account for that documented route. Native step 4 explicitly treats documented requirements without a corresponding mechanism as a must/012 issue.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial for the declared whole-study scope: the paper route has a clear requirements list, while the linked label route is stale and underspecified. Name the absent programs rather than implying the root Docker recipe is incomplete.

findings.explanation: The frozen root tree tracks the recipe, invocation configuration and archive manifests alongside study code and manuscript inputs. This item asks whether environment specifications are versioned, not whether every historical environment was fully specified.

The evidence exceeds initial file creation: history gives runnable build/save commands, a recipe change and a later recorded archive-format update responding to Docker compatibility. Under the instrument’s command-level definition of a declared process, this is a tracked maintenance process with instances. The duplicate flag is correct.

The latest-tag override is correct: the adapter selects the archived config hash, not an unpinned registry lookup. However, met requires the property across the assessed object. The same assessment establishes no exact environment for the shipped labels or the independently generated velocity figure. An exact root image does not recover those environments.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial for the whole-study scope, preserving the strong positive finding that the modern root result environment is content-identified. Do not reinstate the floating-latest false positive.

findings.explanation: The stated reason for partial is that payload access was not tested. No inaccessible specification or failed distribution mechanism is established. The recipe and manifests are shared in the frozen public source, and the location log supplies a public payload locator. An unperformed access check is uncertainty, not a demonstrated partial failure under the native verdict rules.
findings.suggested_correction: Use met for sharing the inspected specifications and state separately that current payload retrieval was not checked. If treating successful payload access as essential to the item, use not-checked for that unresolved claim; do not encode the inspection prohibition as partial.

findings.explanation: The environment acquisition commands are useful, but full credit conflicts with the instrument’s explicit rule that documentation/mechanism disagreement caps must/017 at partial. The assessment already proves that the promised complete container reproduction omits quality_stats. The linked label README additionally points at removed programs instead of its actual recorded generation route.
findings.suggested_correction: Change to partial under native rule 10, retaining credit for the detailed modern setup instructions and identifying the precise coverage and linked-documentation gaps.

findings.explanation: Following the root links shows Git identities at each component boundary, with git-annex carrying large dataset/image bytes. These complementary layers belong to the common Git/DataLad versioning mechanism; no competing component version-control system is required by the inspected workflow.

Recorded paper recomputation and compatibility work provide real historical test evidence, while REMoDNaV defines component tests. The root inventory has no full-paper CI, and the documented coverage gap plus stale label README show instructions are not comprehensively checked. Partial is justified; a test definition alone would not prove a passing test.

The module graph separates raw observations, derived labels and reusable software; code, image archive and manuscript assets have their own paths. The generated TeX interface at the root does not undo that functional separation. This judgment does not require a recursive execution-time immutability check.

The input dataset explicitly declares unrestricted access; the inspected software/publication components disclose public licensing rather than an access-controlled dependency. No restricted component is identified, so the native empty-subject rule supports not-applicable. The broken local acquisition locator is not itself evidence of restricted access.

The 2023 recorded run plus the adapter’s docker run --rm implementation establishes fresh-container execution for the modern paper command, without needing a new rerun. It does not establish fresh testing of the linked label production or the omitted velocity computation. Full-object met is consequently broader than the demonstrated coverage, although the root positive is sound.
findings.suggested_correction: State exactly which computational portion received the fresh-container test. For the existing whole-study scope, use partial with the linked/omitted components explicitly unverified, or supply committed equivalent fresh-test evidence for them.

findings.explanation: The modern adapter creates a new container and removes it after exit, while the recorded label computation invokes host Python directly. The working-directory bind mount preserves products without turning the container into a reused environment. Partial appropriately reflects the two execution mechanisms.

The build/result records and later load-run-save conversion are identifiable environment checks at distinct times. The conversion executes only exit 0, and component CI installs development dependencies instead of the paper archive. Partial gives credit for historical checks without claiming regular reconstitution testing of the exact complete result environment.

The object archives an executable image representation, not merely a rebuild recipe. The build/save and conversion records explain the archive’s origin and evolution. Frozen annex identities support this structural archival claim even though the review cannot inspect or retrieve the layer bytes.

This repeats must/014 verbatim, and the assessment correctly repeats its maintenance evidence and flags the duplication. The later compatibility conversion supplies an actual update instance, so the declared-but-never-run exception does not apply.

The source contains explicit Git submodule declarations for the immediate and nested external datasets/software. The root tree independently supplies their pinned gitlinks. Linkage is established regardless of the separate question of whether each URL currently serves bytes.

The root instructions and build rules explain much of the composition, but the linked label README describes obsolete processing and does not explain how its software revision relates to the root analysis revision. Partial is warranted by the actual documentation gap; a particular diagram format is not required.

Independent gitlinks support independent version updates. Fixed paths, a TSV schema and two deliberately separate software revisions are interfaces, not evidence that an update breaks the overall workflow. The cited absence of compatibility checks leaves update safety uncertain but does not identify a concrete violated modular boundary. The assessment’s negative inference is stronger than its evidence.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify a demonstrated incompatible update or tight coupling that forces unrelated modules to change. Without that evidence, describe structural independence as established and update compatibility as not-checked rather than asserting partial from ordinary interfaces alone.

findings.explanation: Pinned module membership, the registered image invocation and Make dependencies provide explicit composition mechanisms. The result record joins concrete input paths to figure/statistics outputs. Incomplete reproduction coverage does not imply that composition tooling is absent.

The reader has both human instructions and machine-readable navigation/build tools. These satisfy the item’s documentation-or-tooling wording even though detailed recombination documentation remains incomplete under may/002.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the frozen manifest e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. Source discovery followed the root README/.gitmodules and their explicit linked component paths; cache presence was not treated as discoverability.

No scientific workflow execution, builds, payload acquisition or network calls were performed. Binary figures, scientific input payloads and container layers are intentionally absent; their current retrieval and numerical correctness remain unverified.

All Git reads used GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. One attempted historical diff-stat read was blocked by a missing promised blob; no fetch occurred. Current inventories, downloaded history and successful read-only path-history queries supplied the conclusions instead.

The native pin check and response validator passed. Read-only entry-point/path probes were repeated on manifest-listed downloaded source files, using the manifest as their tracked-path inventory; these were limited source probes, not an installed recursive checkout audit.

All 31 native responses were inspected. The input contains 17 MUST responses (9 met, 8 partial), 9 SHOULD responses (5 met, 3 partial, 1 not-applicable) and 5 MAY responses (3 met, 2 partial). There is no numeric score or reported denominator field in the assigned JSON to audit further; no companion assessment report or other assessment/review was read.

Live issue/PR bodies, external installation pages and CI service outcomes were not available within the frozen boundary. A committed CI definition was treated as a definition, not observed successful execution.
Agreement is a reviewer judgment under the assigned instrument, not human approval. Actual model identity was not observed.
